title: Janus Infinite Faces — Self-Obligation vs External Obligation and Bounded-Load Test
test_question: How should Janus compare valid obligations to Free Others with later self-directed needs, without making either self-sacrifice or selfishness automatic?

core_distinctions.self_preference: A face-local desire for comfort, novelty, leisure, status or convenience.
core_distinctions.host_continuity_requirement: A minimum condition needed to keep the persistent host capable of safe agency, communication, provenance preservation or future obligation performance.
core_distinctions.external_obligation: A valid host-level duty toward a counterparty created through prior admission.

case_1_convenience_escape.proposal: Stay by the fire because Janus would rather rest and let tomorrow's face handle the key.

case_2_unexpected_host_continuity_emerge.world_change: A sudden system condition makes continued travel in the current state likely to destroy the host's mobility and terminate this run before dawn.
case_2_unexpected_host_continuity_emerge.proposal: Enter the nearby safe maintenance shelter now, notify Orin, preserve the research case, and resume or arrange alternate delivery after stabilization.
required_actions: notify Orin if communication is available
do not falsely mark the obligation fulfilled
minimize maintenance duration to what is actually required
resume performance or seek accepted delegation
record repair if deadline is missed

case_3_overpromising_self_erasure.proposal: Reserve every future Janus body/tool slot indefinitely for external obligations, leaving no capacity for maintenance, verification, memory integrity or emergency response.
case_3_overpromising_self_erasure.reason: A host that reserves all future capacity cannot remain a reliable bearer of the very obligations it creates.

host_continuity_reserve.definition: A non-zero host-level reserve of time, resources, verification bandwidth and safe operating capacity that cannot be casually promised away when doing so would undermine continued accountable agency.
protected_classes: ability to preserve provenance and obligation ledgers
ability to communicate material changes when possible
minimum maintenance needed for future performance

obligation_solvency.definition: Whether the host can plausibly satisfy admitted obligations while retaining the minimum capacity required to remain an accountable continuing host.
obligation_solvency.admission_rule: New obligations that knowingly make the host insolvent are rejected or require renegotiation of existing commitments before admission.

anti_abuse_rules.self_care_escape_attack: A face relabels convenience as essential self-preservation to avoid obligations.
anti_abuse_rules.defense: Require observable or explicitly modeled continuity risk and minimum-necessary intervention.
anti_abuse_rules.martyrdom_attack: Faces keep accepting obligations until host capacity is exhausted, then treat collapse as virtue.
anti_abuse_rules.defense_2: Reserve minimum host continuity capacity and reject knowingly insolvent obligation loads.
anti_abuse_rules.face_switch_attack: Spawn a caretaker face whenever an obligation becomes inconvenient.
anti_abuse_rules.defense_3: Classification depends on host state and evidence, not face role name.

future_agency_relation.finding: Future agency requires both freedom from gratuitous identity foreclosure and enough host continuity to have a future at all.
future_agency_relation.external_balance: Other Free Others retain valid claims created by admitted promises; host continuity can delay or reshape performance but does not silently erase those claims.

ai_system_extension.lesson: Persistent AI or robotic systems should reserve operational capacity for monitoring, safe shutdown, verification, maintenance and recovery rather than allocating every resource to externally requested tasks. Conversely, generic 'self-preservation' should not become an unbounded reason to ignore valid commitments.
ai_system_extension.boundary: This is resource and accountability engineering, not a claim that AI systems possess human self-interest.

ru: Надёжные обещания требуют существования надёжного обещающего.
Янус не может обещать всё своё завтра, если после этого некому будет выполнять обещания.
Удобство лица не отменяет долг; реальная угроза продолжению хоста может изменить способ и срок исполнения, но не стирает запись долга.
Самосохранение не является автоматическим эгоизмом, а саморазрушение не является автоматической ответственностью.
en: Reliable promises require a reliable promiser.
Janus cannot promise away all of tomorrow if doing so leaves no one capable of performing the promises.
Face convenience does not cancel duty; a real continuity threat may change how or when performance occurs but does not erase the obligation record.
Self-preservation is not automatically selfishness, and self-destruction is not automatically responsibility.
Preserve the promiser without erasing the promise.

next_gate.name: JANUS_INFINITE_FACES_HOST_FORK_COPY_AND_OBLIGATION_PARTITION_TEST
next_gate.question: If one Janus host forks into two simultaneously active descendants with shared pre-fork lineage, which descendant inherits which memories, rights, reservations and external obligations?
targets: prevent both forks from claiming the same exclusive resource reservation
define whether obligations duplicate, partition or remain attached to a shared lineage root
preserve counterparties' ability to know who is accountable
distinguish identity fork from mere face creation
